newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ranariddh seeks U.N. intervention in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh seeks U.N. intervention in Cambodia.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted First Prime Minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, urged the Security Council on Thursday not to recognise any government resulting from last weekend's coup and to order a freeze on aid to Cambodia.
After meeting council President Peter Osvald of Sweden, he told reporters he also asked the council to appeal for mediation in the crisis by King Norodom Sihanouk, now in Beijing.
Ranariddh, Sihanouk's son, was ousted on Sunday by his co-prime minister, Hun Sen, after two days of fighting between their forces in Phnom Penh, the capital.
Sihanouk has already offered to mediate but has been turned down by Hun Sen.
Ranariddh said he had asked for the council "not to recognise any government issued from a coup d'etat and...to do everything in the framework of the Paris peace accord."
That 1991 agreement ended years of civil war in Cambodia and launched a U.N. peacekeeping operation that resulted in elections in 1993.

The council "should make a clear appeal to His Majesty the King for his immediate mediation...because the Paris peace accord says very clearly that the King has to resolve any difficulty and serious crisis in Cambodia," Ranariddh said, adding that mediation would also be in line with Cambodia's constitution.

Ranariddh said he had asked the council to "freeze any assistance and aid to Cambodia unless Cambodia be back not only to normality, but to the framework of the Paris peace accord, that is to say, to have a democratic, liberal state."
He said he was delivering the same message during meetings with General Assembly President Razali Ismail and Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Asked about reports that his supporters intended setting up a rival government in the city of Battambang, he said: "My first priority is to resolve the problem through political and diplomatic means, to place it...clearly in the framework of the Paris peace accord.

"The United Nations is the mother of the Paris peace accord and, (with) the health of the sons going not very well, it is very urgent that the father or the mother must now right away intervene -- not interfere, but intervene."
He welcomed a decision by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), meeting in Kuala Lumpur, to postpone Cambodia's membership and to continue recognising Ranariddh as co-premier.

Ranariddh said he had appealed to ASEAN to "postpone, at least for the time being, the admission of the Kingdom of Cambodia because the regime that will be set up after the coup is illegal and is outside the framework of the Paris peace agreement," of which ASEAN members were signatories.
